theorem.statement: If m>0, the original critical kernel K_alpha=ker(F:C_0->S_(a,b,n-1)) is zero. If m=-d<=0, with d a nonnegative integer, E maps every C_j into C_(j+1), and K_alpha is EXACTLY the kernel of E^(d+1):C_0->C_(d+1). Further, E^j is injective on K_alpha for every 0<=j<=d, with image in C_j. Its explicit left inverse on that image is (d-j)!/(j! d!) times F^j. Consequently dim K_alpha<=dim C_j for every such j; the absence of ANY of these actual lowest types is a sufficient written criterion for both original obstruction multiplicities to vanish.
proof: The Chevalley relation [f_i,e3]=0 and Jacobi imply [f_i,E^j x]=E^j[f_i,x] for i=1,2. Hence E^j preserves actual lowestness in the stated direction. The target C_(d+1) is legitimate for THIS raising map because this commutator was proved; it is not the generally false claim that the original f3 ordinary target is a joint-lowest target.

On S_alpha the previous finite-dimensional root-sl2 theorem gives ker F=0 when m>0, and ker F=ker E^(d+1) when m=-d<=0. Intersect with C_0. Because E^(d+1) maps C_0 into C_(d+1), the displayed map of actual lowest spaces has exactly the original ordinary critical kernel. This is an equality of subspaces, not a character-based rank calculation.

If x belongs to K_alpha, Hx=-d x and Fx=0. The commutator calculation gives F E^t x=t(d-t+1)E^(t-1)x. Iterating for t=1,...,j yields F^j E^j x=j! d!/(d-j)! x. All these coefficients are nonzero in characteristic zero when j<=d. Thus E^j is injective on K_alpha and the inverse scalar shown in the statement is valid. Its images are in the actual C_j by the first paragraph, proving each inequality.

The change in finite-Levi type is forced by the root grading: the lowest h1/h2 weights fall by j, and the longest-element orientation converts these into mu_1+j,mu_2+j. The quotient at level n+j contains every actual relation there; replacing it by a free source or assuming a vanishing type is not allowed.
